content.title: About
content.content: Tofu is a soy curd made from soy milk. In this dish tofu is combined with carrots, broccoli and/or dark‑green leafy vegetables, dressed with a soy‑based sauce. The meal is rich in plant protein, fiber, vitamins and minerals, and contains no potatoes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tofu has a neutral flavor, allowing it to absorb the taste of sauces and spices easily.
Broccoli contains sulforaphane, a compound studied for its potential anti‑cancer properties.
Dark‑green leafy vegetables such as spinach and kale are high in vitamin K and antioxidants.
Soy sauce (2242) is a traditional Japanese condiment produced by fermenting soybeans, wheat, salt and water.
The combination of tofu and vegetables provides a complete set of essential amino acids.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Tofu supplies all essential amino acids, making it a valuable protein source for vegetarians and vegans.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Dark‑green leafy vegetables and soy sauce provide calcium, magnesium and vitamin K, which contribute to bone mineralization.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Broccoli and carrots are abundant in beta‑carotene and vitamin C, helping combat free radicals.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables promotes intestinal motility and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The absence of potatoes and the presence of tofu make the dish suitable for blood‑sugar control.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to soy products, including tofu and soy sauce.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce can be high in salt; people monitoring sodium intake should use it in moderation.

items.title: Phytates
items.content: Soybeans contain phytates, which may reduce the absorption of certain minerals when consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cut tofu into cubes and lightly sauté, then add boiled or steamed vegetables. Drizzle the mixture with soy sauce (2242) and, if desired, sprinkle with sesame seeds. It can be served hot or cold, as a salad topping or as a side dish to grains.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store tofu in an airtight container, covered with fresh water and change the water daily; keep it in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Keep vegetables in a separate bag in the crisper drawer. Soy sauce should be kept in a cool, dark place and refrigerated after opening.
